knowledge.display_text: The study aimed to identify baseline factors longitudinally associated with late-life cognitive decline and examine variation by age and sex.

statements.modality: study aim; not a completed result
conditions: This is the study objective, not a completed empirical result.
statements.temporal_context: Study planning before follow-up analyses

knowledge.display_text: The longitudinal community-based cohort included 1,037 adults aged 70–90 without dementia at baseline.

conditions: Community-dwelling adults aged 70–90 without dementia at baseline.
statements.temporal_context: Baseline recruitment

knowledge.display_text: Of 1,037 baseline participants, 889 completed reassessment at approximately two years; mean follow-up was 23 months and 12 days. Another 43 had died and 105 declined follow-up.

statements.temporal_context: Baseline to the single follow-up; mean 23 months and 12 days

knowledge.display_text: Trained psychology graduates administered neuropsychological tests covering attention/processing speed, memory, language, and executive function.

conditions: Assessments were administered to recruited Sydney cohort participants.
statements.temporal_context: Baseline and follow-up assessment waves

knowledge.display_text: Raw scores were standardized against a baseline cognitively normal, early-English-speaking subgroup (n=504); domain scores averaged component-test z-scores, and global cognition averaged the domain scores.

conditions: Scores were standardized against the specified baseline cognitively normal reference subgroup.
statements.temporal_context: Baseline and follow-up score construction

knowledge.display_text: MCI required a cognitive complaint, objective impairment on at least one test (≥1.5 SD below norms where adjusted norms were available), no DSM-IV dementia, and no or minimal cognitive-related daily-function impairment.

conditions: Bayer ADL score was adjusted for physical impairment.

knowledge.display_text: The study measured candidate sociodemographic, health, lifestyle, smell, and biochemical factors using interviews, questionnaires, examinations, fasting blood assays, and APOE genotyping.

conditions: The described blood assays included cholesterol, homocysteine, and creatinine; this source did not report plasma IL-6 measurement.
statements.temporal_context: Baseline assessment

knowledge.display_text: Longitudinal cognitive change was analyzed with age- and sex-adjusted general linear models; incident MCI/dementia used logistic regression, and models tested age and sex interactions.

conditions: The described models estimate observational associations, not causal effects.
statements.temporal_context: Baseline-to-follow-up analyses

knowledge.display_text: Across the assessed domains, mean cognitive z-scores declined during follow-up; the magnitude differed by domain.

statements.temporal_context: Approximately two years

knowledge.display_text: Among 665 participants classifiable at both waves, 77 developed MCI and 16 developed dementia by follow-up.

knowledge.display_text: The authors caution that risk-factor associations differ across cognitive domains and that inconsistent assignment of tests to domains limits cross-study comparability.

statements.modality: authors' interpretation
conditions: This limitation concerns comparisons of cognitive-domain results across studies with different test batteries.

knowledge.display_text: Interpretation is limited by non-random attrition, self-reported measures, one follow-up at two years, possible diagnostic instability and regression to the mean, untested interactions beyond age and sex, and uncertain generalizability.

conditions: The authors caution that null and unexpected findings should be interpreted carefully.

knowledge.display_text: The authors conclude that associations with late-life cognitive decline vary by age, sex, and outcome; they propose tailored interventions as a possibility requiring future testing.
